Data & Platforms: SONA (University of Oklahoma Psychology Research Pool)
Application Areas: Clinical Assessment of Mental Health Conditions
Structural Equation Modeling and Factor Analysis
Key Research Thinking Patterns: Simulation-Based Robustness Testing: Evaluating the stability of statistical estimators under violated assumptions by generating synthetic data with controlled distributional properties to establish empirical thresholds for bias. (e.g., Monte Carlo simulations of Graded Response Model parameter recovery under varying skew and kurtosis levels)

Dynamic Fit Index Framework Extension: Developing automated, context-specific cutoffs for model fit assessment in complex structures where traditional static benchmarks fail, thereby improving the detection of model misspecification. (e.g., Hierarchical DFI framework achieving >95% classification accuracy in second-order factor models)

Taxonomic Clarification of Researcher Flexibility: Distinguishing between acceptable methodological choices and questionable research practices to reduce ambiguity and heterogeneity in scientific reporting. (e.g., Conceptual and simulated demonstrations redefining Researcher Degrees of Freedom vs. Questionable Research Practices)

Multi-Method Psychometric Evaluation: Integrating Exploratory and Confirmatory Factor Analysis with Item Response Theory to determine optimal factor structures and item-level precision for clinical instruments. (e.g., Comparing eight-factor vs. five-factor models of the Duke Misophonia Questionnaire using EFA, CFA, and MIRT)
Summary Description: Patrick Manapat is a psychometrician specializing in the validation of psychological instruments and the advancement of statistical methodology for structural equation modeling and Item Response Theory. His research focuses on enhancing the reliability and reproducibility of psychological measurement by developing dynamic fit indices for complex factor structures and establishing robustness guidelines for non-normal data distributions. He applies these methodological innovations to validate clinical scales, such as those for misophonia and self-compassion, while simultaneously contributing to meta-science by clarifying researcher degrees of freedom to improve replicability. His work bridges rigorous statistical simulation with practical clinical assessment development.
